title: The Greatest Do Now Ever
author: Adam Boxer
source: Carousel Teaching, Learning, Leading Substack, December 22, 2025
summary: Chronicles how an early-career science teacher named Tom pushed back on departmental Do Now practices, sparking a complete redesign of classroom retrieval and accountability systems. The new system integrates homework flashcards, self-assessment quizzes, in-class quiz checks, and consequences for failing to meet mastery thresholds. Students must prove learning on homework through in-class quizzes tied directly to the same content; cheating becomes nearly impossible due to triangulation between online homework, written exercise book evidence, and class assessment. Low performers are identified quickly and remediated; high performers get success experiences. The system is deceptively simple in execution but complex in thought: it closes the accountability gap between homework and achievement while keeping workload manageable. The author, initially defensive of existing practices, was convinced by the evidence and is now implementing it across his own classes with strong results.
points: Connecting homework directly to in-class assessment via identical quiz content creates accountability that ensures students engage seriously with retrieval practice rather than rushing through it.

The triangulation method (online flashcards, written evidence in exercise books, class Do Now scores) makes cheating nearly impossible while also allowing teachers to diagnose exactly where student confusion lies.
Passmark-based systems with retakes in individual quiz questions allow every student to experience success, improving motivation compared to binary pass-fail structures.
Teachers can tailor difficulty (number of questions, question level, retake limits) to class level, ensuring every student can meet and exceed the passmark.
Rolling out innovation requires iteration across terms, feedback from colleagues, careful consideration of workload, professional training for staff and students, and parent communication.
quotes: Our Do Nows aren't good enough!? Our Do Nows? Not good enough? Who the hell does this child think he is?? We spent years perfecting the routine!

Relying on students working at home is, however, a risky business. Even once students are in good habits around completing the homework, we can always question whether they have actually learnt anything.
Homework is traditionally completed as quickly as possible with minimal cognitive effort. There are lots of reasons for this, but many of them stem from a lack of perceived value in the homework.
Because students are held to account for their performance in a subsequent quiz, they are incentivised to take the retrieval seriously.
Cheating is a thing of the past: students definitely can't cheat on the Do Now in class because of the triangulation between online quiz, flashcards in exercise books and score.

The very structure of the task sets students up for success. Some students sadly don't often get the chance to succeed, but in this case everyone can meet and exceed the passmark.” Archived from Carousel Teaching, Learning, Leading Substack on April 20, 2026 by Tim.
